correctness.rationale: Exact disjoint-partition integration gives \(\phi_1+\phi_2=2\sqrt{\pi}\sqrt{x}\). Positive-argument cumulant ODEs are global and cooperative. The square-root derivative of the sum lies between sqrt(pi) and sqrt(2 pi), giving a nontrivial zero-argument cumulant by monotone limit and genuine finite-time explosion. Bounded phi_2 gives u_2<=2Lt and u_1>=pi t^2-2Lt. This forces both arguments to infinity; hence u_2/t->2L. Differentiation of sqrt(u_1) gives the explicit next-order coefficient 4 sqrt(2 pi L), and the Laplace semigroup yields survival probabilities. The local uniqueness used is only for strictly positive initial arguments; no uniqueness at zero is assumed. Numerical checks were replayed from the included checker; infinite-time proof does not rely on them.

value.rationale: This resolves the specific two-type Lévy-partition example set aside as undecidable by the motivating paper's criteria and identifies opposite tail scales depending on the initial type. The new result is a natural exact classification plus quantitative explosion-time laws, not a routine finite test or parameter renaming. Its sharp leading constants and the \(t^{3/2}\) correction give useful structure for multitype explosion studies.
